title: use-case-spec template variables
description: Values for templates/use-case-spec.md.j2 and templates/use-case-spec.html.j2. Generated by tpl-jinja from use-case-spec.md; `description` on each property is the question put to the author.

error_handling_behavior.title: Error handling behavior
error_handling_behavior.description: The error handling behavior used under 'EX-1'.

goal_sentence.title: Goal sentence
goal_sentence.description: One sentence - what the actor achieves and why they care. It must still read true with the system switched off; a goal that mentions a button is a screen description.

precondition.title: Precondition
precondition.description: A verifiable system state before the flow begins. Verifiable means somebody could query it - "user is authenticated and the claim period is open", not "user is ready".

primary_actor.title: Primary actor
primary_actor.description: The single actor whose goal this satisfies, by role and not by name. If two roles want different outcomes from these steps, you are holding two use cases in one document.

success_postcondition.title: Success postcondition
success_postcondition.description: What is observably true afterwards - the record written, the message emitted, the file produced. Name the thing an automated test could assert on.

trigger.title: Trigger
trigger.description: The event that starts this - a user action, a schedule, an inbound message. Say what is observably true in the instant before step 1.

uc_id.title: Uc id
uc_id.description: The use-case id (UC-014). The traceability matrix points at it, so allocate once and never renumber - a renumbered use case silently orphans every requirement that cited it.

uc_name.title: Uc name
uc_name.description: Verb plus noun from the actor's side - "Submit Expense Claim". Not "Expense Module" and not a screen name; a use case is something a person does, not a place they do it.

uc_xxx.title: Uc xxx
uc_xxx.description: The uc xxx used under 'Related Use Cases'.
